title: Rerank the shortlist, set the cutoff, know when to abstain
brief: Hybrid search returned fifty plausible chunks and the answer needs three. Who decides the order, where do you cut, and what does the system do when nothing is good enough?

blocks.title: The retrieval funnel
blocks.alt: A query goes through recall with BM25 and vector search, fusion with RRF, reranking of the top 50, and a good-enough check that either generates with citations or abstains.
blocks.src:
flowchart LR
  Q[Query] --> R[Recall: BM25 and vector]
  R --> F[Fuse with RRF]
  F --> RR[Rerank top 50]
  RR --> C{Good enough?}
  C -->|yes| G[Generate with citations]
  C -->|no| A[Abstain or fall back]
blocks.caption: Recall decides what can be found. The reranker only reorders what recall supplied.

blocks.title: Rerankers
blocks.intro: A reranker reads the query and each candidate together, so it can judge relevance that embeddings and term counts miss. Late-interaction models (ColBERT style) sit between: they keep token vectors per document and score a cheap interaction, so they can retrieve or rerank at an index size cost [[r12]].

options.name: Azure semantic ranker
options.summary: Managed reranker inside Azure AI Search.
pros: One request, no extra service to run
Returns `@search.rerankerScore` (0 to 4), captions and optional answers
cons: Reranks only the top 50 and cannot find new documents
About 2,000 tokens per document reach summarisation, and the summary string is capped at 2,048 tokens
`orderBy` with semantic ranking returns HTTP 400, and an empty or `*` search string is incompatible with it [[r42]]
options.bestWhen: You already use Azure AI Search and want a managed precision stage.
options.avoidWhen: Candidates must be scored beyond 50 or the text cannot leave your own hardware.

meta.v: premium feature, pay as you go on the standard plan

options.name: Hosted rerank API
options.summary: Send the query and candidates to a vendor model such as Cohere Rerank.
pros: Long context: rerank-v4.0 models take 32k tokens and rerank-v3.5 takes 4096
Accepts structured documents, and Cohere recommends YAML strings
cons: Adds a network hop and a per-query cost
options.bestWhen: You need long or structured candidates and data may go to a vendor.
options.avoidWhen: Residency or egress rules forbid sending chunk text out.

options.name: Self-hosted cross-encoder
options.summary: Run a cross-encoder model on your own GPU or CPU.
pros: You control data path, model choice and fine-tuning
cons: You operate a model service and its scaling
Input length is limited by the model, so long chunks need splitting
options.bestWhen: Data must stay in your network or you want to fine-tune on your own judgements.
options.avoidWhen: You cannot staff a model service and a managed option meets the need.

options.name: LLM reranker
options.summary: Prompt a GPT-class model to order a window of candidates (RankGPT style).
pros: Properly instructed LLMs gave competitive and sometimes better ranking than supervised rerankers on standard benchmarks
Flexible: add domain rules in the prompt
cons: An extra model call per candidate window, so the slowest and costliest
Benchmark contamination is a risk, which is why the authors built NovelEval
options.bestWhen: Latency is relaxed and ranking quality is the top concern.
options.avoidWhen: You need a tight latency budget or high query volume.

blocks.title: Pick a reranking stage
blocks.prompt: Flip the latency budget, the allowed data path and the length of your chunks.

blocks.takeaway: The reranker choice is mostly a data path and latency decision. The ranking quality gap between the options is smaller than the cost of getting those two wrong.

blocks.title: Confidence gates: what to do when the shortlist is weak
blocks.intro: Abstention is a design, not an error path. Pick the cheapest gate that meets the cost of a wrong answer.

options.name: Score cutoff
options.summary: Abstain when the best reranker score is below a coarse threshold.
pros: Easy to monitor as an abstention rate
cons: Brittle when the score distribution drifts
Cannot tell a good partial answer from noise
options.bestWhen: A wrong answer is costly and you can accept some over-abstention.
options.avoidWhen: You have no labelled set to calibrate against.

options.name: CRAG-style evaluator
options.summary: A lightweight evaluator scores retrieved documents and triggers different actions, such as filtering them by decompose-then-recompose or falling back to web search.
pros: Plug and play, no model fine-tuning
cons: An extra model call and a fallback source to govern
Web fallback may be forbidden for private data
options.bestWhen: The corpus is sometimes weak and a safe fallback exists.
options.avoidWhen: Answers must come only from approved internal sources.

options.name: Self-RAG
options.summary: One trained LM decides when to retrieve and critiques passages and its own output with reflection tokens.
pros: Adaptive: skips retrieval when it is not needed
cons: Needs a fine-tuned model (the paper reports 7B and 13B)
Hard to reproduce with a closed hosted model
options.bestWhen: You control the model and can train it.
options.avoidWhen: You call a hosted general model and cannot fine-tune.

options.name: Answerability instruction
options.summary: Tell the model it may say it does not know, and for long documents ask for word-for-word quotes first.
pros: Anthropic guidance recommends explicit permission to say I don't know
cons: The model can still over-claim, so it is not a guarantee
Hard to measure without a check on the answer
options.bestWhen: Used together with a cutoff and a citation check.
options.avoidWhen: It is your only guard in a high-risk domain.

items.symptom: Adding the semantic ranker changed little, and the best document still never appears.
items.cause: It reorders only the top 50 candidates. The document never entered the candidate set.
items.fix: Raise recall first: make `k` plus `maxTextRecallSize` at least 50 and check the document's rank before reranking.

items.symptom: The abstention rate doubled after a service update, with no change on your side.
items.cause: A fixed score cutoff met a shifted reranker score distribution.
items.fix: Use a coarse cutoff, alert on the abstention rate, and re-run the labelled set after updates.

items.symptom: A chunk with the right sentence at its end scores low.
items.cause: Only about 2,000 tokens per document reach the ranker summary, with the title and keywords taking a share.
items.fix: Shorten chunks, move the key facts earlier, and compare scores for a chunk and its sub-chunks.

items.symptom: A sort option added to the request returns HTTP 400.
items.cause: `orderBy` is not allowed with semantic ranking.
items.fix: Remove it and sort client side if the product needs a different order.

quiz.q: Put the stages of a confidence-aware retrieval funnel in order.
items: Retrieve candidates with BM25 and vector search
quiz.explain: Recall comes first because later stages only reorder or drop what recall supplies. Fusion merges the lists before the reranker, which then reads full text. The cutoff needs the reranker's judgement and the model answers last.

quiz.q: After enabling the semantic ranker, a relevant document still never appears. Debug output shows it at BM25 rank 35 and vector rank 40. Which change addresses the cause?
options: Sort the results by `@search.rerankerScore` with an `orderBy` clause
Lower the reranker score threshold that is applied before generation
Request more extractive captions for each candidate document
Raise `k` and `maxTextRecallSize` to sum to at least 50
quiz.explain: With `k` at 10 and `maxTextRecallSize` at 20 the candidate set is at most 30 documents, so rank 35 and 40 never reach the ranker, which takes the top 50. Raise recall, then check again. `orderBy` returns HTTP 400 with semantic ranking, a lower threshold only filters what exists and captions change what is shown, not what is retrieved.

quiz.q: Your abstain cutoff on `@search.rerankerScore` worked at launch. After a service model update the abstention rate doubles. What is the best response?
options: Hard-code a lower number such as 2.4 and move on without monitoring it
Threshold on the RRF score instead, because it does not change between model updates
Keep a coarse cutoff, alert on the abstention rate and recalibrate after updates
Remove the cutoff so that the system always answers every question
quiz.explain: The docs warn that the reranker score distribution shifts with infrastructure and model updates, so use coarse cutoffs and re-test. A new hard-coded number will drift again, the RRF score depends on how many lists and which k you use rather than on relevance, and never abstaining turns weak retrieval into confident wrong answers.

takeaways: A reranker can only reorder the candidates recall gave it, so fix recall first
Choose the reranker by data path and latency before quality
Never threshold on RRF scores, and keep reranker cutoffs coarse because the distribution drifts
Abstention needs a signal, a fallback and a monitored rate
